sections.h2: How big is Aurora, and which counties does it cover?
sections.html:
Aurora straddles the Fox River in northeastern Illinois and ranks second in the state by population, behind only Chicago. The 2020 census found 180,542 residents, and the July 2025 Census estimate is 181,505. No other Illinois city this large lacks a county seat.

It began in Kane County and has since spread into DuPage, Kendall and Will, one of three Illinois cities spanning four counties. For a seller, that decides which recorder files the deed and which treasurer sends the tax bill, so start with the parcel number.

sections.h2: What are the West Side, East Side and Far East Side?
sections.html:
The river splits the city, and each bank has its own story. East Aurora incorporated in 1845 and West Aurora was organized in 1854, and the two merged into one city in 1857. Because neither side would yield, public buildings went up on Stolp Island, in the river itself.

  • The West Side is everything west of the Fox River.
  • The East Side runs east from the river to the DuPage County line.
  • The Far East Side is the part of Aurora beyond that line.

Ten wards divide the city, and the three regions also track police boundaries and school districts. When you describe a house to a buyer, name the side of the river: it signals the school district and often the county in one phrase.

sections.h2: What kinds of older houses does Aurora have?
sections.html:
The Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad kept its roundhouse and locomotive shop in Aurora and was the largest employer until the 1960s. Luxembourgers arrived in numbers between 1850 and 1870, and later waves from Ireland, Britain, Scandinavia and elsewhere filled the neighborhoods near the East Side factories.

Near downtown you find Italianate and Queen Anne houses, with Prairie School homes in the neighborhoods beside the core. The city also counts over 50 Sears Catalog Homes and seven Lustron all-steel houses. Owners of those, or of any pre-1950 house, will hear buyer questions about old wiring, lead paint, aging plumbing and settling foundations.

A cash offer for such a house is usually priced with the repairs in mind, while a listing buyer tends to raise them after the inspection.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Aurora houses?
sections.html:
The answer changes with the address, because several systems share the city.

  • West Aurora District 129 covers the west bank.
  • East Aurora District 131 covers the east bank.
  • Indian Prairie District 204 covers the far eastern portion in DuPage County.
  • Oswego District 308 runs four schools within Aurora's limits, while parts of the far north end go to Batavia schools and a southwestern corner to Kaneland.

The Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy, a state-funded residential school for grades 10 to 12, is in the city, along with Aurora University and two Waubonsee Community College branches. Across the districts, the city has 46 public schools.

sections.h2: Does Aurora's weather and flood history affect a house sale?
sections.html:
It can. Aurora's climate is humid continental, with roughly 40 inches of precipitation a year. A storm on July 17 and 18, 1996 dropped a state-record 16.94 inches of rain in one day, and floodwater reached nearly every low spot and the neighborhoods along the Fox River.

Buyers near the river therefore tend to raise basement moisture, sump pump age and flood insurance. Keep repair invoices handy and answer honestly about past water. Your insurer or the city's engineering staff can tell you whether your parcel sits in a mapped flood zone.

sections.h2: What drives the Aurora economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Manufacturing built the city, and it still sits at the edge of the Illinois Technology and Research Corridor. Caterpillar, Western Electric and Lyon Workspace Products are among the names on its industrial list, and the railroad shops once employed much of the East Side.

The 2022 Economic Census shows $3.12 billion in retail sales and $1.42 billion in health care receipts, and workers spend 27.2 minutes on average getting to their jobs. Downtown has the Paramount Theatre and the Hollywood Casino, and Phillips Park Zoo is also in the city.

  • 72.1% of people 16 and older are in the labor force.
  • 46.4% of residents age 5 and up use another language at home.
  • 26.4% of residents were born outside the United States.

Buyers range from first-time families to investors, so a tidy house on a quiet street draws different interest than a fixer on a busy corner.

sections.h2: What does Aurora's rental licensing mean if my house has tenants?
sections.html:
Each non-owner-occupied unit needs a license and gets inspected once a year, inside and out. The program dates to June 1, 1982, when the city council adopted its Property Maintenance Code. Renewals fall due by August 31, and the Property Standards Division mails renewal forms and schedules inspections by letter.

When a licensed building sells, the code asks for the new owner to be reported to the Operations Department within 3 working days. Property Standards is at 77 S Broadway, 1st Floor, and the licensing line is 630-256-3770. The division also handles high weeds, junk and trash, unsafe stairs, illegal basement apartments and unregistered landlords, and it runs vacant property licensing.

An empty inherited house, or a rental whose tenant has left, can draw a violation notice, so clear those items before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: How are the deed and transfer tax handled on an Aurora sale?
sections.html:
The state's transfer tax is collected as revenue stamps through the recorder of the county where the parcel lies, and the Illinois Department of Revenue notes the same stamp can show payment of a county tax. Buyer and seller sign Form PTAX-203 for filing at that county.

Since Aurora touches four counties, ask the title company which recorder handles your address before you set a signing date, and ask whether any home rule charge applies.

faqs.a: Parts of four: Kane, DuPage, Kendall and Will. The parcel number on your tax bill tells you which one holds your house, records the deed and sends the tax bill.

faqs.q: Does a tenant-occupied house need a license to sell?
faqs.a: The license belongs to the owner who rents the unit and is renewed by August 31 each year. Report the new owner to the Operations Department within 3 working days after a sale, and call Property Standards at 630-256-3770 with account questions.

faqs.q: Will past flooding hurt the sale?
faqs.a: It can, mainly because buyers worry about repeat water. Tell them about past problems, keep repair records, and mention any sump pump or drainage work. Near the Fox River, expect flood insurance to come up.

faqs.q: Can a house with open code violations be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, and many buyers take houses as-is. Still, find out what is open at your address before you sign anything. Property Standards can explain what it takes to close a case.

faqs.q: Listing or cash offer: how do I decide?
faqs.a: Compare take-home money and timing. A listing may reach a higher price but adds repairs, showings and loan risk, while a cash purchase trades some price for a faster, steadier closing.
